mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP growth above 3% over a 6-month horizon signals accelerating economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth exceeds 3% for 6 months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index below its 12-month moving average by more than 2% signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If industrial production falls below its 12-month moving average by more than 2% but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over a 3-month horizon signals a tightening monetary cycle, which increases discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: If the federal funds rate rises above 4.5% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

failure_condition: If the unemployment rate rises above 8% for 6 months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.
